title: Sparse-coalesce KV compactness evaluation and fidelity guardrails
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Goal: Evaluate a sparse-coalesce approach to KV cache compactness that groups small contiguous KV slices before quantizing, then measure fidelity trade-offs across FP8/INT8/INT4 encodings under continuous batching workloads. We want to determine whether coalescing offers better memory+latency economics than per-shard quantization and derive conservative guardrails for rollout (fallback thresholds, cohorting, rollback triggers).
background: We have many prior KV quantization probes (per-shard, blockwise, hybrid) but continuous batching exposes many small KV writes/reads that inflate metadata overhead and limit packing efficiency. The sparse-coalesce idea: during continuous batching windows, detect temporally-adjacent KV appends for the same token cohorts and coalesce them into a single contiguous block before applying a shared quantization scale or low-bit packing. This reduces per-entry headers and improves pack density, potentially enabling safe use of INT8/INT4 for cohorts that would otherwise be noisy at single-entry quantization. We need end-to-end validation: model fidelity (perplexity/log-probs, classification/regression tests), latency/throughput under production batching distribution, and GPU memory reduction numbers.
experiment_plan: Phase 0: Synthetic bench to validate packing density and encode/decode overhead across FP32 baseline, simulated FP8, INT8, and INT4 variants without coalesce
Phase 1: Implement sparse-coalesce encoder for runtime (in a feature flag) with a heuristic: coalesce contiguous entries for same request origin if cumulative size < 256KB or time delta < 120ms
Phase 2: Run live shadow traffic (1%) against representative continuous-batching profiles: chat-short, chat-long, completion-heavy with Zipf token distribution sampling
Phase 3: Offline fidelity evals: perplexity delta, MRR, and reranking AUC on curated prompt sets. Include adversarial prompts to detect worst-case quantization artifacts.
Phase 4: Latency and tail SLO analysis: measure P50/P90/P99 token latency and end-to-end request P99 under coalesced quantization vs baseline

Phase 5: Safety guardrails: determine thresholds for automatic fallback to higher-fidelity storage (FP8 or FP32) based on cohort drift, recent error residuals, and observed downstream regression counts
metrics_to_capture: Memory delta (GPU DRAM) per model shard and aggregated across serving pool
Packing density (bytes payload / bytes stored) and header overhead reduction
Model fidelity: average log-prob delta, perplexity change, downstream eval metric regression counts
Latency: additional encode/decode CPU cost, P50/P90/P99 token latency impact
Throughput: requests/sec change under same GPU utilization
Rollback triggers: number of cohorts crossing fidelity thresholds per hour
success_criteria: >30% reduction in KV storage footprint at INT8 packing with coalesce vs per-entry INT8 baseline, or >2x density improvement vs uncompressed FP32
Model fidelity: no more than 0.5% relative regression on key downstream metrics (MRR/perplexity) for production cohorts, and clear explanation for any regressions
Latency P99 increase < 10ms attributable to encode/decode for typical request sizes
Safe fallback policy defined and tested: automatic per-cohort reversion to FP8/FP32 when residuals exceed threshold for 3 consecutive windows
Operational observability: Grafana dashboard + anomaly alerting for cohort fidelity, memory pressure, and encoding errors
implementation_notes: Encoder implemented as a runtime feature-flagged path (kv_pack.coalesce = true). Keep original per-entry store intact until canary finishes so we can 'replay decode' for safety checks.
Coalesce heuristic parameters are runtime-configurable via feature gate; start conservative and expose to Dedicated customers as opt-in
Use a shared scale-per-coalesced-block for INT8/INT4 to reduce quantization noise from tiny entries
Instrumentation: attach a lightweight checksum/residual per block to detect silent corruption from packing/quantization
Integrate with batching controller to surface coalescing stats per batch window
current_findings: Synthetic bench: coalescing increases pack density by 1.8x-2.3x depending on batch mix; encode/decode CPU overhead ~4-6% on a single CPU core for typical block sizes (<=128KB)
INT8 with coalesce shows average log-prob delta of +0.8% on chat-short set, while INT4 shows +3.6% (unacceptable for high-fidelity cohorts)
FP8 (E4B) with coalesce gives memory reduction similar to INT8 in many cases but with consistently lower fidelity delta (~0.4%)
Tail latency: P99 increased by ~6ms in the service that decodes coalesced blocks; optimization possible by moving decode to native kernel and using SIMD paths
Observed one case where adversarial token sequence caused INT4 coalesced block to amplify token-wise bias; added a per-block residual monitor to detect this pattern
open_risks: Cohort selection: coalescing across heterogeneous cohorts can mask per-request differences and amplify quantization bias
Operational complexity: new storage format increases downgrade/upgrade complexity for rolling deploys and cross-version compatibility
SLO exposures: encoding CPU overhead could push a microservice into resource saturation under high concurrency
Silent degradation: if residual checks are too loose, small systematic quality loss may accumulate before detection
mitigations: Default to FP8 coalesced blocks for production cohorts and reserve INT8/INT4 only for low-fidelity cohorts (embeddings, reranking warm caches)
Implement automatic cohort fencing: do not coalesce across user segments with heterogenous traffic patterns
Expose a conservative runtime knob to disable coalescing per-route or per-model; surface in Console as 'KV compactness' toggle
Add per-block rolling residual windows and integrate with Redwood Optimize to suggest quantization profile changes when drift observed
